question: Which type of line is used to represent hidden edges or surfaces in a technical drawing, as per BIS SP 46-2003?
solution:
The correct answer is __Dashed thin line**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dashed thin line__ is used to represent hidden edges or surfaces in technical drawings.
 
• As per BIS SP 46-2003, specific line types are standardized for clarity in technical drawings.
 
• Hidden edges and surfaces are not directly visible in the 2D representation of a 3D object.
 
• Dashed thin lines help identify the concealed features without ambiguity.
 
• These lines improve the readability and comprehension of technical designs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Continuous Thin Line:**

 
 
• Used for dimension lines, projection lines, and leader lines.
 
 
 
• **Chain Thin Line:**
 
 
• Represents center lines, lines of symmetry, and trajectories.
 
 
 
• **Continuous Thick Line:**
 
 
• Used for visible outlines and edges.
